title: Dried alginate‐chitosan‐based capsules containing cauliflower microgreens: physicochemical properties and stability
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis) microgreens are rich in bioactive phytochemicals, but the high lability of these compounds limits their shelf life. To determine their viability as functional ingredients, this study evaluated how three dried capsule systems produced by ionic gelation affected the physicochemical properties, molecular interactions, and preservation of bioactive compounds compared with unencapsulated microgreen powder (MCG). The systems evaluated were alginate capsules (ALG), chitosan-coated alginate capsules (ALG-CH), and alginate capsules coated with modified low-molecular-weight chitosan (ALG-MCH).

RESULTS

Encapsulation efficiency ranged from 60.7% to 74.9%. Relative to MCG, the capsules showed measurable color changes and markedly improved flowability (the Hausner ratio decreased from 1.61 to 1.04), whereas ALG capsules were more hygroscopic. Chitosan-coated capsules exhibited greater swelling at 1 h, followed by a decrease at 6 h, whereas ALG capsules remained stable. Infrared spectroscopy combined with multivariate analysis distinguished the wall materials: chitosan amide (1595 and 1538 cm⁻1) and methyl (1418 cm⁻1) bands distinguished chitosan-coated capsules from plain alginate capsules, consistent with alginate–chitosan electrostatic complexation, and further distinguished modified from unmodified chitosan coatings. Under accelerated storage conditions (35–70 °C), total phenolic content decreased according to zero-order kinetics in all systems. ALG had the highest activation energy (29.04 kJ mol⁻1) and longest half-life at 35 °C (53 days), versus ALG-MCH (50 days) and ALG-CH (42 days). Positive activation free energy (ΔG‡) and negative activation entropy (ΔS‡) values indicated a substantial kinetic barrier and an association-type degradation mechanism.

CONCLUSION

Alginate encapsulation was the most effective in preserving phenolic stability, indicating its potential as a nutraceutical carrier. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
